items.readable_text:
Content:
The second-order Cauchy-Euler equation has the form
[MATH: ax^2y''+bxy'+cy=f(x),]

Content:
where [MATH: a,b,] and [MATH: c] are constants.

Content:
Cauchy-Euler equations can be solved using a trial solution [MATH: y=x^\lambda,] where [MATH: \lambda] is a constant to be found. To illustrate, let's solve the following Cauchy-Euler equation:

Content:
[MATH: x^2y''+xy'-9y=0]

Content:
Differentiating the trial solution [MATH: y = x^\lambda] with respect to [MATH: x] gives

Content:
[MATH: y' = \lambda x^{\lambda -1}, \qquad y'' = \lambda(\lambda-1)x^{\lambda-2}.]

Content:
Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

Content:
[MATH: x^{2}λ(λ − 1)x^{λ − 2} + xλx^{λ − 1} − 9x^{λ}|= 0; λ(λ − 1)x^{λ} + λx^{λ} − 9x^{λ}|= 0; x^{λ}(λ(λ − 1) + λ − 9)|= 0.]

Content:
So, we have the following characteristic equation:

Content:
[MATH: λ(λ − 1) + λ − 9|= 0; λ^{2} − 9|= 0; λ|= ± 3]

Content:
Therefore, the general solution is

Content:
[MATH: y(x)|= c_{1}x^{3} + c_{2}x^{− 3}; = c_{1}x^{3} + (c_{2})/(x^{3}).]

  • Equation III is not a Cauchy-Euler equation because the [MATH: y''] term is not multiplied by an [MATH: x^2.]

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

sections.normalized_html: Find the general solution to the equation [MATH: 3t^2 y''+8ty' -2y = 0, \quad t\gt 0.]
sections.readable_text:
Find the general solution to the equation
[MATH: 3t^2 y''+8ty' -2y = 0, \quad t\gt 0.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
This is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume the solutions take the form [MATH: y=t^\lambda.] Differentiating [MATH: y] with respect to [MATH: t] gives

[MATH: y' = \lambda t^{\lambda -1}, \qquad y'' = \lambda(\lambda-1)t^{\lambda-2}.]

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

[MATH: 3t^{2} ⋅ λ(λ − 1)t^{λ − 2} + 8t ⋅ λt^{λ − 1} − 2t^{λ}|= 0; 3λ(λ − 1)t^{λ} + 8λt^{λ} − 2t^{λ}|= 0; t^{λ}[3λ(λ − 1) + 8λ − 2]|= 0.]

So, we have the following characteristic equation: [MATH: 3λ(λ − 1) + 8λ − 2|= 0; 3λ^{2} + 5λ − 2|= 0; (λ + 2)(3λ − 1)|= 0]

The roots of the characteristic equation are [MATH: \lambda = -2] and [MATH: \lambda = \dfrac{1}{3}.] Therefore, the general solution is [MATH: y(t)|= c_{1}t^{− 2} + c_{2}t^{1/3}; = (c_{1})/(t^{2}) + c_{2}t^{1/3}.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
We find the constants [MATH: c_1] and [MATH: c_2] using the initial conditions.

  • First, we apply the condition [MATH: y(1)=0.] Substituting [MATH: y(1)= 0] into the general solution gives [MATH: 0 = c_1+c_2 \quad \Rightarrow \quad c_2 = -c_1.]

  • Then, we apply the condition [MATH: y'(1) = 5.] Differentiating [MATH: y,] we get [MATH: y^{′}|= − 3(c_{1})/(x^{4}) + 2c_{2}x.] Substituting [MATH: y'(1)=5] and [MATH: c_2=-c_1] into the above gives [MATH: 5|= − 3c_{1} + 2c_{2}; 5|= − 3c_{1} + 2(− c_{1}); 5|= − 5c_{1}; c_{1}|= − 1⇒c_{2} = 1.]

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is [MATH: y(x)=x^{2}-\dfrac{1}{x^3}.]

[MATH: x^2 y'' +2 xy' -6 y= 0, \quad y(1)= 0, \quad y'(1) = 5, \quad x \gt 0.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We find the constants [MATH: c_1] and [MATH: c_2] using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition [MATH: y(1)=0.] Substituting [MATH: y(1)= 0] into the general solution gives
[MATH: 0 = c_1+c_2 \quad \Rightarrow \quad c_2 = -c_1.]
- Then, we apply the condition [MATH: y'(1) = 5.] Differentiating [MATH: y,] we get
[MATH: y^{′}|= − 3(c_{1})/(x^{4}) + 2c_{2}x.]
Substituting [MATH: y'(1)=5] and [MATH: c_2=-c_1] into the above gives
[MATH: 5|= − 3c_{1} + 2c_{2}; 5|= − 3c_{1} + 2(− c_{1}); 5|= − 5c_{1}; c_{1}|= − 1⇒c_{2} = 1.]

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is
[MATH: y(x)=x^{2}-\dfrac{1}{x^3}.]
